findings.recommendation: `customer_label` calls `db.customer(invoice.customer_id)` (src/report.rs:39, `SELECT ... FROM customers WHERE id = $1`) once per invoice: one query for the list plus one per invoice, so about 3 000 queries for a month of 3 000 invoices from only 800 customers, growing linearly with invoice volume. Collect the distinct `customer_id`s, fetch them once with the existing batch method `db.customers(&ids)` (`WHERE id = ANY($1)`), index them in a `HashMap<i64, Customer>` and build each label from the map. Keep the invoice-number order and return an error when an id is missing, as `db.customer` does today.
findings.title: One customer query per invoice in the monthly report

findings.recommendation: `purchase_order` is called for every invoice of the month (src/report.rs:28) and compiles the same pattern on each call: about 3 000 regex compilations per report, a cost far above the match itself and growing with invoice volume. Compile it once — a `static PO: std::sync::OnceLock<Regex>` (or `LazyLock`) — or build it in `monthly_report` before the loop and pass it in.
findings.title: The purchase-order regex is compiled once per invoice
